name: East Australian Current
scope: Coherent poleward shelf-break jet from about 15 degrees S to the usual separation around 32 degrees S; excludes Tasman Front and downstream eddy/extension routes.
layer: Jet geographic description; no velocity layer or depth integration diagnosed.
time_convention: General geographic reference sketch; not the instantaneous model surface-speed snapshot in Figure 1 or a dated observed centerline.
source_locator: Section 1 Introduction, opening paragraph (15 degrees S to usual separation around 32 degrees S); Figure 1 for regional orientation only.
source_citation: Reilly et al. (2026), Two-tier MOM6 regional modelling suite of the East Australian Current system, Geoscientific Model Development 19, 3853-3873, doi:10.5194/gmd-19-3853-2026.
coordinate_selection: OSW chooses coarse offshore waypoints to sketch the east Australian shelf-break corridor. The source supplies latitude limits and flow description, not these longitudes, intermediate vertices, or a numerical current length. These vertices are not digitized model data or published coordinates.
scenario_rule: Three uniform route longitude offsets (-0.25, 0, +0.25 degrees), crossed with independent start and end latitude offsets (-0.5, 0, +0.5 degrees): 27 finite editorial scenarios. Offsets are OSW choices, not source-reported uncertainty. Intermediate latitude gates stay fixed. Does not span all possible meanders or branch choices. A preliminary -0.5 degree westward route crossed the coarse atlas land mask near 28 degrees S; it was rejected rather than included as a plausible route.
remaining_gates: Inspect correspondence with a sourced shelf-break/bathymetric corridor, beyond the coarse atlas land mask.
Review northern origin and separation conventions against alternative geographic accounts.
Independent physical-oceanography review of the nominal route and scenario choices.
Integrate separately scoped candidate geometry and measurement into canonical release and atlas pages before public admission.
source_retrieval_note: Source passage rechecked 2026-10-03 for protocol migration; original retrieval date was not recorded. Geometry and length unchanged.
